title: SSE reconnect + chunk-framing robustness for streaming API
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Hardening the streaming response surface: implement an SSE-first server implementation that normalizes chunk framing, exposes deterministic reconnect semantics (resume tokens + token offsets), and provides a compatibility shim for historical chunked-transfer consumers. This ticket covers protocol design, runtime server changes, end-to-end tests, and a transitional compatibility mode for SDKs still using legacy chunk boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits well-formed SSE events for all streaming responses (event: data, id optional per-message, "retry" where useful)

Chunk framing guarantees: every semantic unit (complete JSON object for structured output or tool-calling boundary) is emitted as a single SSE data field; large payloads are split only at safe byte boundaries with reassembly metadata

Reconnect semantics supported: clients can reconnect with last_seen_id and byte_offset to resume without duplicating function/tool calls; server validates resume tokens and resumes from KV-cache where applicable
Compatibility shim toggled by header (X-Redwood-Stream-Mode: legacy|sse) so older clients retain current behavior while new SDKs adopt SSE-normalized framing
Automated integration tests simulate flaky networks (mid-stream disconnect, out-of-order chunks) and assert idempotent tool-calling and no silent truncation of structured outputs
implementation_notes: Design choice: prefer SSE for browser-first clients and native HTTP streaming for SDKs — normalize server output to SSE event frames as canonical; add header-based compatibility layer
Resume token format: base64 of (model_version|request_id|sequence_number) signed with server key; include byte_offset for partially emitted large data
On reconnect, server checks resume token TTL and KV cache availability; if cache miss, fallback to re-generation with deterministic checkpointing or fallthrough policy
Chunk framing rule: ensure JSON structural boundaries (object/array) are not split across independent SSE data events unless accompanied by sequence metadata for reassembly
Tool/function call guard: treat tool invocation as a commit point — do not re-invoke tools after resume; mark invoked tools in durable request-scoped state
qa_plan: Unit tests for framing utility: boundary insertion, safe-split algorithm, reassembly logic
Integration tests with test harness that injects deterministic disconnects at token N and asserts resume correctness
Fuzz tests for various content-lengths and binary payloads in structured outputs
Manual verification with browser SDK, node SDK, and python SDK against legacy and sse modes
Load test to verify new framing does not regress latency or throughput under continuous batching profiles
rollback_plan: Feature toggle controlled by X-Redwood-Stream-Mode header; immediately start serving legacy mode for failing clients
Runtime config killswitch (global) to revert to existing chunked-transfer behavior within 2 minutes
Instrumentation to detect higher-than-baseline duplicate tool invocations and silent truncation, with alerting to oncall
